scenarios.title: Dropping files from Finder onto a pane types their shell-escaped paths at the cursor without Enter
scenarios.summary: Finder-to-pane drop is a drag between two app windows, and the harness drags only within one window.

scenarios.title: Text copied in another macOS app pastes into a pane with ⌘V, bracketed only when the program asked for it
scenarios.summary: Cmd+V never pastes: Quirky toasts 'Could not paste ... user denied permission' or WebKit shows its own Paste callout, and nothing reaches the pane.

scenarios.title: ⌘-clicking a URL in a pane opens it in the system browser, and Reveal in Finder on a file link shows it in Finder
scenarios.summary: The harness can't Cmd-click. The popover's Open sent the exact URL to the system browser and Reveal in Finder selected notes.txt, both confirmed only by screen capture.

scenarios.title: In the desktop window, ⌘R renames the tab and never reloads the webview; under Terminal first ⌘T reaches the terminal and opens no tab
scenarios.summary: App first: Cmd+T opens a tab and Cmd+R opens the rename field with no reload; Terminal first: Cmd+T and Cmd+Shift+T open no tab and Cmd+D still splits.

scenarios.title: In the desktop window, visible panes render with WebGL (at most 12 contexts) and the memory probe at the typical-day workload stays within budget
scenarios.summary: No in-window report of WebGL contexts or mounted xterms, and the memory probe isn't in this worktree.
